fact_check.claim: 'Linea got the partnership with Swift, which is something that XRP was supposed to do, which is why Linea is one of my community favorites'; Linea 'was 64 million' market cap and 'isn't too bad for the monthly' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: CORRECTED. Swift announced in September 2025 that it is building a blockchain shared ledger with Consensys, the company that built Linea, and Consensys CEO Joe Lubin said publicly that it is being built on Linea. The ledger went into a live pilot on July 9, 2026 with 17 banks (BNY, Citi, Wells Fargo, BNP Paribas, HSBC, Lloyds, Standard Chartered, UBS, ANZ, DBS, MUFG, OCBC, UOB, First Abu Dhabi Bank, Mashreq, Itau Unibanco, FirstRand). The live ledger runs on a permissioned Hyperledger Besu network built by Consensys: 'Linea-family in lineage but not the public Linea network'. So copy says 'Swift picked Consensys, the team that built Linea, to build its blockchain ledger' and never that Swift runs on Linea or uses the $LINEA token. $LINEA UPDATED: $0.00289, about a $71M cap, rank 382, +2.6% 7d, +11.4% 30d. 'Swift was supposed to be the $XRP story' is Mike's commentary. persona project_handles linea = null, so no Follow line.

fact_check.claim: 'Coinbase and Citigroup expanded their partnership on the 28th to bridge traditional banking and blockchain infrastructure; the integration allows merchants to accept stablecoins without holding or managing the digital assets, as Coinbase handles the blockchain transaction and the conversion'; 'why doesn't Coinbase just become a bank?'; the stablecoin-yield drama on centralized exchanges (transcript, a video Mike saw)
fact_check.verdict: verified. Sept 28, 2026: Citi and Coinbase expanded the partnership first announced in October 2025. Citi's institutional clients can accept stablecoin payments through Spring by Citi with Coinbase running the stablecoin rails and converting to fiat while Citi settles as the bank of record; Coinbase Virtual Accounts run on Citi's Virtual Account Wallet; US first; the companies cite more than 150 million stablecoin holders. Added context for Mike's bank question: the OCC gave Coinbase conditional approval for a national trust charter on April 2, 2026 (a trust charter, no retail deposits), so the tweet says 'already has conditional approval for a national trust charter' before asking why it does not go all the way. The stablecoin-yield fight is NOT used (its current status was not verified).

fact_check.claim: 'Bitcoin posts a 42.7% Q3 gain, best since 2017'; 'Bitcoin surges 40% in its best quarter since late 2024' (transcript, headlines Mike read)
fact_check.verdict: verified and recomputed. Coinbase: June 30 close $58,523.93 to Sept 30 close $83,556.14 = +42.8%; press figure +42.71%, the best third quarter since 2017 (+80.41%) and the second-best Q3 on record (Q3 2013 +40.6%, Q3 2025 +6.31%). First half of 2026: $87,497.94 (Dec 31 close) to $58,523.93 = about -33%. The 2026 low is $57,717.55 on July 1 (Coinbase daily lows from Oct 2025 through Oct 5, 2026); ATH $126,296 on Oct 6, 2025. Copy: 'best third quarter since 2017, up about 43%', 'second-best Q3 ever', 'lost about a third of its value in the first half', 'printed its low on July 1 at about $57.7K'. 'Best quarter since late 2024' is NOT used: sources disagree on which quarter it beats.

fact_check.claim: 'US Treasury yields post worst fourth quarter since 1994, when the stock market started to go on that run, the dot com run' (transcript, a headline Mike read)
fact_check.verdict: verified with one correction: it is the THIRD quarter of 2026. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 87.1 basis points in Q3 to just under 5.28%, the sharpest quarterly rise since 1994 (Reuters: 'US Treasuries' worst quarter since 1994'); the 30-year reached 5.65%, the highest since 2002. Copy: 'Treasuries had their worst selloff since 1994', 'the 10-year yield jumped about 87 basis points to roughly 5.28%'. Mike's dot-com parallel is not used.

fact_check.claim: Cycle history: the first Bitcoin cycle ran two and a half years from inception to a June 2011 top; the second ran two and a half years to a December 2013 top; the cycle that topped in 2017 was the first four-year cycle, 'absolutely boring for the first three years', then parabolic from Q3 into December; the first cycle had one mid-cycle top, the second had two, the third had none (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: dates verified, mid-cycle counts trimmed. Genesis block Jan 3, 2009; top near $32 in June 2011 (about 29 months); top near $1,150 to $1,200 in late 2013 (sources date it Nov 30 or Dec 4, so copy says 'late 2013'; about 30 months); top near $20K in December 2017 (48 months). Q3 2017 returned +80.41%. Only the spring 2013 mid-cycle top is written (documented: Bitcoin crossed $100 that spring before the late-2013 run past $1,000); 'the first cycle had one, the second had two, the third had none' is not used. 'Three of those four years were dead boring' is Mike's read. 'I shed my four-year cycle belief in Q2 2025' is persona core_theses.

fact_check.claim: 'Bitcoin has closed October in the green 77% of the time'; October opened at 83K; 'I think we're going into a bull trap and there's going to be a correction', not 'to a new bottom, like 56K let alone 38K... maybe go down to like 75'; the four-year cycle zombies 'were waiting for an October bottom'; a bearish divergence on Bitcoin (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified where checkable. 10 of 13 Octobers since 2013 closed green = 76.9% (red: 2014, 2018, 2025). October 2026 open $83,556.14 (Coinbase). $BTC $85,952 on 2026-10-05, +4.2% 7d. The pullback toward $75K is Mike's own scenario and is written 'I still think a pullback comes first, maybe toward $75K. Not a new low.' The bull trap already shipped as a full YT post and thread on 2026-10-03, so it gets one tweet of thread 2 with the new $75K level instead of its own item. Persona core_theses honored: the zombies are written as having October circled for a bottom that printed three months earlier; no copy says they cause a bottom in October. The bearish divergence is not used (a chart read that cannot be checked here).

tweets.text:
Bitcoin ($BTC) just posted its best third quarter since 2017: up about 43%.

Now everybody wants to compare this run to 2017.

Fine. Let's actually look at 2017, because it is where the whole four-year cycle story comes from...
tweets.hook: Bitcoin ($BTC) just posted its best third quarter since 2017: up about 43%.

tweets.text:
Cycle one: Bitcoin's first block in January 2009 to the top in June 2011. About two and a half years.

Cycle two: that June 2011 top to the top in late 2013. About two and a half years again, with a mid-cycle top in the spring of 2013 along the way.

Cycle three is the one everybody remembers: late 2013 to December 2017.

That was the FIRST four-year cycle. Three of those four years were dead boring. Then Q3 2017 printed about +80% and the whole thing went parabolic into December.

So the four-year cycle is not a law of Bitcoin. The first two cycles ran about two and a half years each.

One cycle stretched to four years and a whole generation of traders built a religion on it. I shed my four-year cycle belief in Q2 2025.

This year the four-year cycle zombies had October circled for the bottom.

$BTC lost about a third of its value in the first half, printed its low on July 1 at about $57.7K, then ran about 43% in Q3.

The low came three months before their date.

And it did that in the same quarter Treasuries had their worst selloff since 1994: the 10-year yield jumped about 87 basis points to roughly 5.28%.

Bonds were bleeding and Bitcoin had its second-best Q3 ever.

Is this 2017 again? Not yet.

$BTC has closed October green in 10 of the last 13 years, so everybody is leaning the same way. It opened the month at about $83,556.

I still think a pullback comes first, maybe toward $75K. Not a new low. Forget $56K, forget $38K.

If this made you rethink the four-year cycle...

Follow me for the macro read that ignores the echo chamber.

🧠

yt_posts.body:
I went through my entire meme watchlist on stream this week, and almost everything more than three weeks old is dying. I counted about five charts that are not.

Here is how I tell a retracement from a rug, and why one of those five is Golden Kitty ($GOLDEN).

Start with what a new meme does right now. It launches, it pumps for a day or two, and by day four or five most of them are dead. Anything can go up on day one, so day one tells you nothing. I would not touch a brand-new launch with a 10-foot pole in this market.

So I run one simple filter: show me a chart that is more than three weeks old and still has buyers. Across my whole list, that was about five memes. Even the bigger caps are retracing. Cash Cat ($CASHCAT), the flagship meme of Robinhood Chain, is about half off its Sept 3 high and down about 36% on the month.

Then the second rule. People call everything a rug. I do not. A meme that is 86% off its high is completely normal; that is what memes do between runs. I do not use the word rug until a chart is 97% down. Above that line it can still come back and take out its all-time high, and I have watched it happen.

Now run Golden Kitty through both rules. It launched Sept 4, so it is a month old. It topped at a little over a $6M cap on Sept 27, and it is about half off that high this week, at around a $3M cap. By my rules that is a retracement, nowhere near a rug.

And here is the part I like most. Look at who is behind it: a lot of influencers and a lot of Discords, all buying it and all pushing it. It is dispersed. It is not one guy who can dump his bag and crash the chart.

If you want to play it safer, go bigger cap. But if the market starts flying over the next couple of weeks, the memes that are still standing are the ones that run. To me that is a chance to get into something that is not dying, at a discount. Never financial advice.

So tell me in the comments: if you had $500 for one meme right now, do you buy the month-old chart that is half off its high, or the one that launched this week?

Click that like button and click the subscribe button if you want the meme reads before the crowd shows up.
